text:
julia: FYI customer (alan-customer) reporting embeddings are suddenly much slower and some requests 503ing. They say requests target eu-west-1 but backend logs show hits to us-east-1. request ids: r_8f3, r_8f4
alan-customer: yep, been seeing 600-1200ms -> 2-6s p95 and occasional 503s. We haven't changed client config. Our env var REGION=eu-west-1.
mike: thanks — can you paste one raw request header/response (no PII) and the SDK region in use? Also roughly the QPS/batch size?
alan-customer: SDK v2.1.3, region set to eu-west-1, qps ~40, batch_size=16. Here header: `X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1`, response trace shows downstream to vecsvc-us-east-1.
raj: sounds like sticky routing + capacity spillover. When eu-west pool is saturated we allow overflow to other regions; should be auto-fallback only when capacity/timeouts happen, but sticky session mapping might still route some tokens to old mappings.
sara: can you repro with sdk verbose logs? try toggling `prefer_local_region: true` in the client config and send a small batch (size 1) — that should force region pin. If that pins and latency improves, it's routing-related.
julia: reproduced here with their headers: small single embeddings hit eu-west and p95 ~90ms; larger 16-batch goes to us-east and p95 ~2.3s. Also saw a few dimension mismatch errors for one vector (customer model expects 1536 but client sent 2048) — but that seems separate.
mike: important: dimension mismatch -> immediate 400 from vecsvc, spills/slowdown -> routing. We need to separate these in ticket and confirm fallback policy triggers.
raj: digging into routing table now. I see an old pin for alan-customer from yesterday (during a eu-west incident) that pinned to us-east while warm-up was happening. Pin TTL should be 10m but one failed cleanup left it sticky. That would explain stray requests after pool recovered.
sara: ops action: clear pin for org alan-customer, force re-eval of route. Also add log marker to show fallback reason (capacity vs error).
mike: queued an urgent deploy to add a safer TTL fallback and prevent pin retention on error. deploy-bot: deploy started for change id cd-5234 to routing-service.
julia: customer tried after pin clear: batch 16 now routed to eu-west and p95 120ms, no 503. They still saw one 400 from dimension mismatch — they fixed client config to correct 1536 dims.
alan-customer: confirmed, performance back to normal after your fix + adjusting dims. Thanks. One ask: can you expose a `X-Redwood-Routing` header so clients can know which region served the request? Would help debugging.
raj: good suggestion — we already emit `X-Redwood-Node` but not region. I'll add `X-Redwood-Region` to responses for embeddings (low risk).
sara: follow-ups: 1) postmortem entry, 2) add metric for pin-ttl-failures, 3) doc note on batching causing cross-region fallback when local capacity hits threshold.
mike: I'll open a support kb with repro steps (toggle prefer_local_region, small batch vs large batch, sample headers) and link to PR.
julia: marking resolved for customer. Leaving this thread for tracking until deploy completes and metric added. :thumbsup:
